title: Finite monic factorization data descends in a filtered colimit of pairs
statement: Let Λ be a nonempty directed preorder, F : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat a diagram with colimit A [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and Jᵢ compatible ideals. Suppose I is an ideal of A whose elements are exactly the images of elements of the Jᵢ. Given a monic polynomial f over A and coprime monic polynomials g₀,h₀ over A/I with f mod I = g₀h₀, there exist a stage i and monic polynomials Fᵢ,Gᵢ,Hᵢ over F(i) such that Fᵢ maps to f, the reductions of Gᵢ,Hᵢ modulo Jᵢ are coprime and multiply to Fᵢ mod Jᵢ, and the images of Gᵢ,Hᵢ modulo I are g₀,h₀. No stage pair is assumed henselian.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0FWT, proof, second paragraph (finite descent before applying henselianity)

proof.text: Use Concrete.colimit_exists_rep for every coefficient in a finite set and Finset.exists_le to move its representatives to a common stage. Apply Polynomial.lifts_iff_coeff_lifts and Polynomial.lifts_and_natDegree_eq_and_monic to lift a finite family of polynomials simultaneously, preserving monicity whenever required. The Mathlib monic-lifting theorem includes the zero-ring case.

For a stage element whose image belongs to I, use hI to choose an ideal representative. Concrete.colimit_exists_of_rep_eq makes the representatives equal at a common later stage, where ideal compatibility gives membership. For a finite family of polynomials vanishing modulo I, apply this to their finitely many nonzero coefficients, take one common upper bound also dominating the original stage, and use compatibility again. Every coefficient then vanishes modulo the ideal at that stage.

Lift the prescribed monic quotient factors to monic polynomials over A using Polynomial.lifts_and_natDegree_eq_and_monic and quotient-map surjectivity. Lift the two Bezout witnesses using Polynomial.map_surjective. Apply step 1 to the five polynomials f,g,h,a,b. Apply step 2 to the two polynomials F-GH and AG+BH-1. At the resulting stage their zero reductions give the factorization and the Bezout identity; transition maps preserve monicity, and cocone naturality gives the prescribed images. This uniform argument also handles zero colimit or quotient rings without assuming nontriviality.

lean.statement:
theorem filteredColimit_factorization_descent
    {Λ : Type u} [Preorder Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty Λ]
    (F : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [HasColimit F]
    (J : ∀ i : Λ, Ideal (F.obj i))
    (hJ : ∀ {i j : Λ} (f : i ⟶ j), Ideal.map (F.map f).hom (J i) ≤ J j)
    (I : Ideal (colimit F : CommRingCat.{u}))
    (hI : ∀ x, x ∈ I ↔
      ∃ (i : Λ) (a : F.obj i), (colimit.ι F i).hom a = x ∧ a ∈ J i)
    (f : (colimit F : CommRingCat.{u})[X]) (hf : f.Monic)
    (g₀ h₀ : ((colimit F : CommRingCat.{u}) ⧸ I)[X])
    (hg₀ : g₀.Monic) (hh₀ : h₀.Monic) (hcop : IsCoprime g₀ h₀)
    (hfact : f.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g₀ * h₀) :
    ∃ (i : Λ) (fᵢ gᵢ hᵢ : (F.obj i)[X]),
      fᵢ.Monic ∧ gᵢ.Monic ∧ hᵢ.Monic ∧ fᵢ.map (colimit.ι F i).hom = f ∧
      IsCoprime (gᵢ.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J i))) (hᵢ.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J i))) ∧
      fᵢ.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J i)) =
        gᵢ.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J i)) * hᵢ.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J i)) ∧
      (gᵢ.map (colimit.ι F i).hom).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g₀ ∧
      (hᵢ.map (colimit.ι F i).hom).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = h₀

blueprint_update.statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a nonempty directed preorder and $i\mapsto A_i$ a functor from $\Lambda$ to commutative rings with colimit $A=\varinjlim_iA_i$ and coprojections $\iota_i:A_i\to A$. Let $J_i\subseteq A_i$ be ideals with $A_i\to A_j$ mapping $J_i$ into $J_j$ for $i\le j$, and let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal whose elements are exactly the elements $\iota_i(a)$ with $i\in\Lambda$ and $a\in J_i$. Let $f\in A[X]$ be monic and $g_0,h_0\in(A/I)[X]$ coprime monic polynomials with $f\bmod I=g_0h_0$. Then there are a stage $i$ and monic polynomials $f_i,g_i,h_i\in A_i[X]$ such that $\iota_i(f_i)=f$, the reductions of $g_i$ and $h_i$ modulo $J_i$ are coprime and their product is $f_i\bmod J_i$, and the images of $\iota_i(g_i)$ and $\iota_i(h_i)$ modulo $I$ are $g_0$ and $h_0$. No pair $(A_i,J_i)$ is assumed henselian.

proof.text: *Lifting finitely many polynomials.* Every element of the filtered colimit $A$ is $\iota_i(a)$ for some $i$ and $a\in A_i$, and since $\Lambda$ is directed, finitely many elements can be represented at one common stage. Applying this to the finitely many coefficients of a finite family of polynomials over $A$ gives a stage $i$ and polynomials over $A_i$ mapping to them. A monic polynomial of degree $d$ can be lifted to a monic polynomial of degree $d$, by lifting its coefficients in degrees $<d$ and taking leading coefficient $1$. This also covers the case $A=0$.

*Vanishing modulo the ideals at a later stage.* Let $a\in A_i$ with $\iota_i(a)\in I$. By hypothesis $\iota_i(a)=\iota_k(c)$ for some $k$ and $c\in J_k$. Two representatives with the same image in $A$ become equal at a common later stage $l\ge i,k$, and there the image of $c$ lies in $J_l$ by compatibility of the ideals, so the image of $a$ in $A_l$ lies in $J_l$. For a finite family of polynomials over $A_i$ whose images in $A[X]$ vanish modulo $I$, apply this to their finitely many nonzero coefficients and take one common upper bound $l\ge i$ of the resulting stages; using compatibility once more, at that stage every coefficient lies in $J_l$, i.e. the polynomials vanish modulo $J_l$.

*Conclusion.* Lift $g_0$ and $h_0$ to monic polynomials $g,h\in A[X]$, using surjectivity of $A\to A/I$ and the monic lifting above, and lift Bezout witnesses $a_0,b_0\in(A/I)[X]$ with $a_0g_0+b_0h_0=1$ to polynomials $a,b\in A[X]$. Apply the first step to the five polynomials $f,g,h,a,b$: there are a stage $i$, monic $f_i,g_i,h_i\in A_i[X]$ and $a_i,b_i\in A_i[X]$ mapping to $f,g,h,a,b$. The polynomials $f_i-g_ih_i$ and $a_ig_i+b_ih_i-1$ map to $f-gh$ and $ag+bh-1$, which vanish modulo $I$ because $f\bmod I=g_0h_0$ and $a_0g_0+b_0h_0=1$. Apply the second step to these two polynomials and pass to the resulting later stage. There their reductions modulo $J$ vanish, which gives the factorization $f_i\equiv g_ih_i$ and the Bezout identity $a_ig_i+b_ih_i\equiv1$, so the reductions of $g_i$ and $h_i$ are coprime with product $f_i\bmod J_i$. Transition maps preserve monicity, and compatibility of the coprojections gives $\iota_i(f_i)=f$ and that $\iota_i(g_i)$, $\iota_i(h_i)$ reduce to $g_0$, $h_0$ modulo $I$. The argument also handles a zero colimit or zero quotient ring without assuming nontriviality.
